subproblem.title: Positive density forces membership in the support (general fact G2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), y ∈ U and θ ∈ ℝ with θ > 0. If Θ^n(μ_T, y) = θ in the sense HasMassDensity T y θ (θ ≥ 0 and M_{B_t(y)}(T)/(ω_n t^n) → θ in [0, ∞] as t ↓ 0, ω_n = unitBallVolume n), then y ∈ spt T.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (y : Euclid P) (θ : ℝ), y ∈ U → 0 < θ → HasMassDensity T y θ → y ∈ T.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. General fact (G2) of the supplied proof of codim1_region_density_one_dense (section ‘General facts’). Only frozen definitions are used:
- spt T = T.support = U ∖ Z(T), where Z(T) = T.zeroRegion is the union of the open W with compact closure in U on which T vanishes. T.VanishesOn W means T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
- M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W}. The admissible ω are the ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(z)) ≤ 1 for all z.
- HasMassDensity T y θ means 0 ≤ θ and M_{B_t(y)}(T)/(ω_n·ofReal(t^n)) → ofReal θ in [0, ∞] along the filter 𝓝[>]0. Here ω_n = unitBallVolume n.

Proof.
1. Suppose y ∉ spt T. As y ∈ U and spt T = U ∖ Z(T), y ∈ Z(T). So there is an open W ∋ y, with compact closure in U, such that T(ω) = 0 whenever ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W.
2. Choose r > 0 with B_r(y) ⊆ W and let 0 < t < r. Every ω admissible for M_{B_t(y)}(T) has tsupport ω ⊆ B_t(y) ⊆ W, so T(ω) = 0 and ofReal(T(ω)) = 0. Hence the set whose supremum defines M_{B_t(y)}(T) is contained in {0}, and M_{B_t(y)}(T) = 0.
3. So M_{B_t(y)}(T)/(ω_n·ofReal(t^n)) = 0 for every t ∈ (0, r), because 0 divided by any element of [0, ∞] is 0. Since (0, r) ∈ 𝓝[>]0, the ratio is eventually 0 along 𝓝[>]0 and therefore tends to 0.
4. By hypothesis the same ratio tends to ofReal θ along 𝓝[>]0. This filter is non-trivial and [0, ∞] is Hausdorff, so limits are unique and ofReal θ = 0, i.e. θ ≤ 0. This contradicts θ > 0, so y ∈ spt T. ∎
proof_key_steps: If y ∈ U ∖ spt T, then y lies in an open W on which T vanishes.
For balls B_t(y) ⊆ W every admissible form has T(ω) = 0, so M_{B_t(y)}(T) = 0.
The density ratio is eventually 0 along t ↓ 0, so by uniqueness of limits ofReal θ = 0, contradicting θ > 0.

subproblem.title: Countably n-rectifiable sets of finite measure have density one almost everywhere (general fact G7; Simon Ch. 3, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5(3), 1.6)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, and let M ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set that is countably n-rectifiable with H^n(M) < ∞ (H^n = μHE[n]). Then H^n(M ∩ B_t(w))/(ω_n t^n) → 1 in [0, ∞] as t ↓ 0 for H^n-almost every w ∈ M (ω_n = unitBallVolume n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), 1 ≤ n → MeasurableSet M → CountablyRectifiable n M → μHE[n] M ≠ ∞ → ∀ᵐ w ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => μHE[n] (M ∩ ball w t) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. General fact (G7) of the supplied proof, cited there from Simon Ch. 3, 1.8(2) and 1.9. For a set of finite H^n-measure (multiplicity θ ≡ 1) these reduce to the following printed items, copied here with the omitted details supplied:
- Lemma 1.2, ‘only if’ (chapter-03.txt lines 25–66);
- Remark 1.3 (lines 67–76);
- the proof of Theorem 1.6 ‘⇒’ (lines 109–144);
- Remark 1.5(3) (lines 91–100).

Notation.
- H^n = μHE[n]. It is isometry invariant, H^n(λA) = λ^n H^n(A), and it equals Lebesgue measure L^n on ℝ^n and on n-planes.
- ω_n = unitBallVolume n.
- η_{w,r}(z) = r^{-1}(z − w) (SimonGMT blowUpMap).
- An n-dimensional subspace Q is an approximate tangent space of M at w (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4; HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M w Q) if ∫_{η_{w,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).

Proof.
1. (Lemma 1.2, ‘only if’: a C¹ cover.)
- By countable n-rectifiability, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} F_j(ℝ^n) with H^n(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^P Lipschitz.
- Fix j. Apply the C¹ Approximation Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5; chapter-02.txt line 165) to the P coordinates of F_j. For each i ≥ 1 this gives a C¹ map G_{ij} : ℝ^n → ℝ^P with L^n({F_j ≠ G_{ij}}) < 1/i.
- Put Z_j := ℝ^n ∖ ⋃_i {F_j = G_{ij}}. Then L^n(Z_j) ≤ 1/i for every i, so L^n(Z_j) = 0. E_j := F_j(Z_j) satisfies H^n(E_j) ≤ Lip(F_j)^n L^n(Z_j) = 0. Thus F_j(ℝ^n) ⊆ E_j ∪ ⋃_i G_{ij}(ℝ^n).
- Let C_{ij} := {z : DG_{ij}(z) not injective}, a closed set on which the Jacobian J_{G_{ij}} vanishes. By the area formula for C¹ (locally Lipschitz) maps (Simon Ch. 2, §3: ∫ H⁰(A ∩ G^{-1}(y)) dH^n(y) = ∫_A J_G dL^n; cf. SimonGMT Chapter02/AreaCritical), H^n(G_{ij}(C_{ij})) = 0.
- Let z ∉ C_{ij}. Apply the inverse function theorem to G_{ij} followed by the orthogonal projection onto DG_{ij}(z)(ℝ^n). This gives an open ball B_z ∋ z, with closure in ℝ^n ∖ C_{ij}, such that G_{ij} is a C¹ embedding near closure B_z: injective, a homeomorphism onto its image, with injective derivative. Moreover H^n(G_{ij}(B_z)) ≤ Lip(G_{ij}|closure B_z)^n L^n(B_z) < ∞.
- By Lindelöf, countably many such balls cover ℝ^n ∖ C_{ij}.
- Altogether M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_{k≥1} N_k, where N₀ := M₀ ∪ ⋃_j E_j ∪ ⋃_{i,j} G_{ij}(C_{ij}) is H^n-null. Each N_k = g_k(B_k) is the image of an open ball under a C¹ embedding g_k defined near closure B_k, is σ-compact (hence Borel), and has H^n(N_k) < ∞.
2. (Remark 1.3.) Put M_k := (M ∩ N_k) ∖ ⋃_{1≤i<k} N_i for k ≥ 1. These are pairwise disjoint Borel sets with M_k ⊆ N_k, and M ∖ ⋃_k M_k ⊆ N₀ is H^n-null.
3. (Tangent planes of the C¹ pieces.) Fix k and w = g_k(z) ∈ N_k, and let T_wN_k := Dg_k(z)(ℝ^n), an n-dimensional subspace.
- g_k is a homeomorphism of B_k onto N_k with injective derivative at z. So there are ρ₀, c, s > 0 with |g_k(z′) − w| ≥ c|z′ − z| for z′ ∈ B_{ρ₀}(z) ⊆ B_k, and N_k ∩ B_s(w) ⊆ g_k(B_{ρ₀}(z)).
- Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) vanish outside B_R(0) and let r < s/R. By the area formula and the substitution z′ = z + ra, ∫_{η_{w,r}(N_k)} f dH^n = ∫ f(r^{-1}(g_k(z + ra) − w))·J_{g_k}(z + ra) dL^n(a). The integrand vanishes for |a| > R/c.
- As r ↓ 0, r^{-1}(g_k(z + ra) − w) → Dg_k(z)a uniformly for |a| ≤ R/c, and J_{g_k}(z + ra) → J_{g_k}(z). By dominated convergence the integral tends to ∫ f(Dg_k(z)a) J_{g_k}(z) da = ∫_{T_wN_k} f dH^n (area formula for the linear map Dg_k(z)).
4. (Proof of Theorem 1.6 ‘⇒’.) Fix k ≥ 1, f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with f = 0 outside B_R(0), w ∈ M_k and r > 0. Since M = M_k ⊔ (M ∖ M_k) and N_k = M_k ⊔ (N_k ∖ M_k),
 ∫_{η_{w,r}(M)} f dH^n = ∫_{η_{w,r}(N_k)} f dH^n − ∫_{η_{w,r}(N_k∖M_k)} f dH^n + ∫_{η_{w,r}(M∖M_k)} f dH^n.
- By step 3 the first term tends to ∫_{T_wN_k} f dH^n.
- For Borel A with H^n(A) < ∞: |∫_{η_{w,r}(A)} f dH^n| ≤ sup|f|·r^{-n}H^n(A ∩ B_{rR}(w)) = sup|f|·R^n(rR)^{-n}H^n(A ∩ B_{rR}(w)).
- By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; chapter-01.txt line 700), applied to the finite Borel regular measure H^n⌞A, ρ^{-n}H^n(A ∩ B_ρ(w)) → 0 for H^n-a.e. w ∉ A. The accepted Submission.regcomp_atl_upper_density_zero states this with closed balls.
- Apply this to A = M ∖ M_k and A = N_k ∖ M_k. Both are Borel, have finite measure, and are disjoint from M_k. The exceptional null sets do not depend on f or R, so for H^n-a.e. w ∈ M_k both error terms tend to 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).
- Hence T_wN_k is an approximate tangent space of M at H^n-a.e. w ∈ M_k. Since M ∖ ⋃_k M_k is null, M has an approximate tangent space at H^n-a.e. w ∈ M.
5. (Remark 1.5(3): density one at approximate tangent points.) Let w ∈ M have approximate tangent space Q.
- H^n(M ∩ closedBall(w, 1)) ≤ H^n(M) < ∞. So the accepted lemma Submission.rsd_tendsto_closedBall_density_of_approxTangent gives H^n(M ∩ closedBall(w, t))/(ω_n t^n) → 1 as t ↓ 0. Its proof is Simon's: squeeze 1_{closedBall(0,1)} between continuous cut-offs g_ε ≤ 1 ≤ h_ε supported in B_1(0) and B_{1+ε}(0), with g_ε = 1 on closedBall(0, 1 − ε). Then use H^n(Q ∩ B_ρ(0)) = ω_n ρ^n and H^n(η_{w,t}(A)) = t^{-n}H^n(A).
- The accepted Submission.rsd_tendsto_ball_density_of_closedBall converts this to open balls, using closedBall(w, (1−ε)t) ⊆ B_t(w) ⊆ closedBall(w, t). Hence H^n(M ∩ B_t(w))/(ω_n t^n) → 1.
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 5, the set of w ∈ M at which H^n(M ∩ B_t(w))/(ω_n·ofReal(t^n)) does not tend to 1 along t → 0⁺ is H^n-null. μHE[n].restrict M has the same null sets inside M and gives measure 0 to the complement of M. This is the asserted ∀ᵐ statement (n ≥ 1 is not needed beyond fixing the setting). ∎
proof_key_steps: Lemma 1.2: the C¹ approximation theorem covers M, up to an H^n-null set, by countably many C¹ n-dimensional embedded pieces N_k of finite measure. Remark 1.3 makes the pieces M_k ⊆ N_k disjoint and Borel.
Each C¹ piece has the approximate tangent space Dg_k(z)(ℝ^n) at every point (area formula plus blow-up).
Proof of 1.6 ‘⇒’: the Upper Density Theorem kills the contributions of M ∖ M_k and N_k ∖ M_k at H^n-a.e. w ∈ M_k, so M has approximate tangent spaces a.e.
Remark 1.5(3), via the accepted rsd_tendsto_closedBall_density_of_approxTangent and rsd_tendsto_ball_density_of_closedBall: at approximate tangent points the open-ball density ratio tends to 1.

subproblem.title: Positive mass on every open neighbourhood of a support point (general fact G3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), W ⊆ ℝ^P open and x ∈ W with x ∈ spt T. Then M_W(T) > 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → x ∈ W → x ∈ T.support → 0 < T.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. General fact (G3) of the supplied proof of codim1_region_density_one_dense. Definitions as in the frozen contract:
- spt T = U ∖ Z(T), with Z(T) = ⋃{W′ open : closure W′ compact, closure W′ ⊆ U, T vanishes on W′}.
- M_W(T) = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(z)| ≤ 1 ∀z}.
- |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I increasing} α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}. Each α ↦ α(e_I) is linear and continuous, so |·| is continuous and |cα| = |c|·|α| (see also the accepted Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props).

Proof.
1. T does not vanish on W. Suppose it did. Since x ∈ spt T ⊆ U and U ∩ W is open and contains x, there is r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ⊆ U ∩ W. Put W₀ := B_r(x). Then W₀ is open, and closure W₀ = closedBall(x, r) is compact (finite dimension) and contained in U. T vanishes on W₀, since every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W₀ has tsupport ω ⊆ W. Hence W₀ ⊆ Z(T) and x ∈ Z(T), contradicting x ∈ spt T = U ∖ Z(T).
2. By step 1 there is ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and T(ω) ≠ 0. The function z ↦ |ω(z)| is continuous (ω is smooth) and vanishes off the compact set tsupport ω. Let s := sup_z |ω(z)| ∈ [0, ∞).
3. Case s > 0. Put c := sgn(T(ω))/s and ω′ := c·ω.
- ω′ ∈ 𝒟^n(U), since 𝒟^n(U) is a vector space.
- tsupport ω′ ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W.
- |ω′(z)| = |c|·|ω(z)| ≤ 1.
So ω′ is admissible for M_W(T). By linearity T(ω′) = c·T(ω) = |T(ω)|/s > 0, hence M_W(T) ≥ ofReal(|T(ω)|/s) > 0.
4. Case s = 0. For every k ∈ ℕ the form ω_k := k·sgn(T(ω))·ω is admissible, since |ω_k(z)| = 0, and T(ω_k) = k·|T(ω)|. So M_W(T) ≥ ofReal(k|T(ω)|) for every k, i.e. M_W(T) = ∞ > 0.
5. In both cases 0 < M_W(T). ∎
proof_key_steps: If T vanished on W, a small ball about x with compact closure in U ∩ W would lie in Z(T), contradicting x ∈ spt T.
Pick ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and T(ω) ≠ 0, and let s = max|ω|.
Rescaling ω (by sgn(T(ω))/s, or by arbitrary multiples if s = 0) gives admissible forms with positive value, so M_W(T) > 0.

audit.reason: The stronger open-neighbourhood statement is justified by shrinking inside U ∩ W. Compact support bounds the coefficient norm, and the two rescaling cases establish positive mass without assuming norm definiteness.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. De Giorgi's theorem in the form used by step 4 of the supplied proof. Book items:
- Simon Ch. 3, 4.1–4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 555–746);
- the BV representation Ch. 2, 2.1–2.2, and Ch. 2, 2.5–2.6 (chapter-02.txt lines 477–626);
- the Riesz theorem Ch. 1, 4.14 (chapter-01.txt line 1654);
- Ch. 1, 3.3, 3.23 and 3.24 (lines 602, 1063, 1125).
The printed first sentence of the proof (line 604, ‘By 1.6 and 3.6 of Ch. 1 the first part follows from 4.3(†)’) is expanded in steps 5–8. There, μ_F = H^m⌞∂*F uses the sibling rectifiable_density_one.
Errata applied:
- the OCR of 4.1 drops the minus sign of the inward-normal Gauss–Green formula;
- the limit set (9) is {z^{m+1} > c} for the inward normal e_{m+1}, consistent with 4.3(‡).

Notation. L^{m+1} = volume = μHE[m+1]; H^m = μHE[m]; ω_k = L^k(B_1); div φ = trace Dφ. The hypothesis applied to −φ gives |∫_F div φ| ≤ C_K.

Proof.
1. (Extension of the functional.)
- For compact K ⊆ D fix d > 0 with K′ := {dist(·, K) ≤ d} ⊆ D.
- If g is C¹ with tsupport g ⊆ K and |g| ≤ 1, the mollifications g_ε (ε < d) are smooth, supported in K′, have |g_ε| ≤ 1, and div g_ε → div g uniformly. Hence |∫_F div g| ≤ C_{K′}.
- So Λ(g) := −∫_F div g satisfies |Λ(g)| ≤ C_{K′} sup|g| for C¹ g supported in K. By uniform density of smooth fields with supports in K′, Λ extends uniquely to C_c(D; ℝ^{m+1}) with the same bound.
2. (Riesz representation; Ch. 2, 2.1–2.2 and 4.1.)
- Simon Ch. 1, 4.14 (X = D, H = ℝ^{m+1}) gives a Radon measure μ_F on D and a μ_F-measurable ν with |ν| = 1 μ_F-a.e. and Λ(g) = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ_F. So
 (4.1) ∫_F div g = −∫_D ⟨g, ν⟩ dμ_F for g ∈ C¹_c(D; ℝ^{m+1}), and the same holds for Lipschitz g by mollification.
- μ_F(W) = sup{Λ(g) : |g| ≤ 1, spt g ⊆ W} for open W, so μ_F(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ D.
- Take ν Borel with |ν| = 1 on D.
3. (Reduced boundary; 4.2.)
- ∂*F is the set of y ∈ D ∩ spt μ_F at which ν_F(y) := lim_{ρ↓0} μ_F(B_ρ(y))^{-1}∫_{B_ρ(y)} ν dμ_F exists and |ν_F(y)| = 1.
- By differentiation of Radon measures (Simon 3.23; Mathlib VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average), the averages tend to ν(y) for μ_F-a.e. y. Hence μ_F(D ∖ ∂*F) = 0 and ν_F = ν μ_F-a.e.
4. (Blow-up; printed proof of 4.3.)
- Fix y ∈ ∂*F. After a rigid motion assume y = 0 and ν_F(0) = e_{m+1}. Put F_λ := λ^{-1}F, μ_λ(A) := λ^{-m}μ_F(λA) and ν_λ(z) := ν(λz); (4.1) holds for F_λ.
- (1)–(2): ⨍_{B_ρ} ν^{m+1} dμ_F → 1 and ⨍_{B_ρ}|ν^i| dμ_F → 0 for i ≤ m.
- (3)–(6): test (4.1) with g = ζ_k e_{m+1}, ζ_k radial Lipschitz cut-offs decreasing to 1_{closedBall_ρ}. Then ∫_{closedBall_ρ} ν^{m+1} dμ_F ≤ (d/dρ)L^{m+1}(F ∩ B_ρ) ≤ H^m(∂B_ρ) for a.e. small ρ. With (1): μ_F(B_ρ) ≤ 2(d/dρ)L^{m+1}(F ∩ B_ρ) ≤ 2(m+1)ω_{m+1}ρ^m for ρ < ρ₁, so μ_λ(B_R) ≤ CR^m.
- (7): BV compactness (Ch. 2, 2.6) gives, along any λ_k ↓ 0, a subsequence with 1_{F_{λ_k}} → 1_{F₀} in L¹_loc.
- (8): for ζ ∈ C¹_c and i ≤ m, |∫_{F_λ} D_iζ| ≤ sup|ζ|·λ^{-m}∫_{B_{λR}}|ν^i| dμ_F → 0. So F₀ = ℝ^m × H. For ζ ≥ 0, (4.1) and (1) give ∫_{F₀} D_{m+1}ζ = lim(−∫ζν_λ^{m+1} dμ_λ) ≤ 0. Hence 1_H is non-decreasing and (9) F₀ = {z^{m+1} > c}.
- (10)–(11): the Sobolev inequality for BV functions comes from Mathlib lintegral_pow_le_pow_lintegral_fderiv by mollification (Ch. 2, 2.5); D(ζ1_F) = ζD1_F + 1_F Dζ. With (6) it gives V^{m/(m+1)} ≤ c(d/dρ)V for V(ρ) = L^{m+1}(F ∩ B_ρ) > 0 (positive because 0 ∈ spt μ_F). So L^{m+1}(F ∩ B_ρ) ≥ c″ρ^{m+1}. The same holds for the complement (normal −ν). These scale-invariant bounds pass to F₀ and force c = 0. Since the limit is unique, 1_{F_λ} → 1_{{z^{m+1}>0}} in L¹_loc (4.3(‡)).
- (12) Put P := {z^{m+1} = 0} = ν_F(0)^⊥.
 * By (4.1) and L¹_loc convergence, ν_λμ_λ → e_{m+1}H^m⌞P weakly.
 * For any weak subsequential limit μ* of μ_λ (which exists by (6)), H^m⌞P ≤ μ*, since the variation of a weak limit is at most the limit of the variations.
 * Testing with ζe_{m+1}, 1_{B_R} ≤ ζ ≤ 1_{B_{R+ε}}, and using (1): ∫(1 − ν_λ^{m+1}) dμ_λ → 0 on B_{R+ε}. So liminf μ_λ(B_R) ≤ ω_m(R+ε)^m, hence μ*(B_R) ≤ ω_m R^m = H^m⌞P(B_R).
 * Therefore μ* = H^m⌞P and μ_λ → H^m⌞P (4.3(†)). In particular Θ^m(μ_F, y) = 1 for open and closed balls, and the cone {dist(z, ℝν_F) ≤ |z|/2} carries μ_λ-mass o(1) in B_1.
5. (Comparison with H^m.)
(a) For A ⊆ ∂*F and open V ⊇ A, Simon 3.3 (t = 1) gives H^m(A) ≤ μ_F(V). So H^m(A) ≤ μ_F(A) for Borel A, μ_F-null subsets of ∂*F are H^m-null, and H^m(∂*F ∩ K) < ∞.
(b) For Borel A ⊆ ∂*F, μ_F(A) ≤ 2^{m+1}H^m(A).
- Let A_k := {y ∈ A : μ_F(closedBall(y, r)) ≤ 2ω_m r^m for 0 < r < 1/k}.
- Cover A_k by sets C_j of diameter < δ < 1/(2k), meeting A_k at points a_j, with Σω_m(diam C_j/2)^m ≤ H^m_δ(A_k) + ε.
- Then μ_F(A_k) ≤ Σ 2ω_m(diam C_j)^m = 2^{m+1}Σω_m(diam C_j/2)^m. Let ε, δ → 0 and then k → ∞.
(c) Choose a Borel B₁ ⊆ ∂*F with μ_F(D ∖ B₁) = 0 (Borel regularity); then H^m(∂*F ∖ B₁) = 0. By (a) and (b), μ_F = θ·H^m⌞B₁ on D, where 1 ≤ θ ≤ 2^{m+1} is Borel and θ(y) = lim μ_F(B_ρ(y))/H^m(B₁ ∩ B_ρ(y)) H^m-a.e. on B₁ (Radon–Nikodym, Simon 3.24 / Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv).

- For an open ball W with closure in D, run that proof with μ := μ_F⌞(B₁ ∩ W) and normal lines π_y = ℝν_F(y).
- It uses only finiteness of μ, density (5) = 1 and the cone condition (6) at μ-a.e. point (both from step 4(12), since μ = μ_F near points of B₁ ∩ W), Lusin/Egoroff, finitely many reference lines, and Lipschitz extension (Ch. 2, 1.2).
- This yields Lipschitz F_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} covering μ-almost all of B₁ ∩ W, and by 5(a) H^m-almost all of it. Hence B₁ is countably m-rectifiable.
7. (θ = 1.) For such W, M_W := B₁ ∩ W is Borel and rectifiable with H^m(M_W) < ∞.

subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, N ⊆ ℝ^P an embedded C² submanifold of dimension n+1 (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) N) with orientation ξN (IsOrientation (n+1) N ξN), and x ∈ N ∩ U. Then there are a linear isometry ι : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P, a map u : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P and reals δ₁, δ₂ > 0 with the following properties.
- closedBall(x, δ₁ + δ₂) ⊆ U, u(0) = 0, and u is C² on D := B_{δ₁}(0).
- For every v ∈ D: u(v) ⊥ ι(ℝ^{n+1}), ‖Du(v)‖ ≤ 1, ‖u(v)‖ < δ₂/2, and G(v) := x + ι v + u(v) ∈ N.
- For every v ∈ D and every (n+1)-covector α: ξN(G(v))(α)·J(v) = α(DG(v)e_1, …, DG(v)e_{n+1}), where DG(v) = ι + Du(v) and J(v) = (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩])^{1/2}.
- Whenever ‖v‖ < δ₁, ‖h‖ < δ₂, h ⊥ ι(ℝ^{n+1}) and x + ι v + h ∈ N, then h = u(v).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 1, (1a)–(1f), of the supplied proof of codim1_region_density_one_dense. It uses the C² embedded-submanifold definition of Simon Ch. 2, §4 and the orientation definition 6.2.2. Here it is stated for an arbitrary x ∈ N ∩ U, with the plane Π parametrised by an isometry ι. Siblings used: orientation_sign and unit_orientation_dual (accepted, reused).

Notation. e_1, …, e_{n+1} is the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1}. ι* is the adjoint of ι, so ι*ι = id and ι*h = 0 iff h ⊥ range ι. DG(v) := ι + Du(v) and J(v) := (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩])^{1/2}.

Proof.
1. (Tangent plane and ι; (1a).)
- IsOrientation at x gives a subspace Π with Π = tangentSpace(N, x) as sets, and an orthonormal τ = (τ_1, …, τ_{n+1}) spanning Π with ξN(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξN(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α.
- In the second case replace τ_1 by −τ_1. This keeps τ orthonormal with the same span, and α(−τ_1, τ_2, …) = −α(τ). So ξN(x)(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_{n+1}) for all α, and dim Π = n + 1.
- Let ι be the linear isometry with ι(e_i) = τ_i; its range is Π.
2. (The chart is a homeomorphism; (1b).)
- IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) N at x gives open V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} and open W ∋ x, and ψ with: ψ C² and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective on V. Fix z₀ ∈ V with ψ(z₀) = x.
- Claim: if C ⊆ V is relatively closed, then ψ(C) is closed in W. Let c_k ∈ C with ψ(c_k) → q ∈ W. Then K := {q} ∪ {ψ(c_k)} is a compact subset of W, so the c_k lie in the compact set V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K). A subsequence converges to some c ∈ V; c ∈ C, and ψ(c) = q.
- So ψ : V → W ∩ N is a closed continuous bijection, i.e. a homeomorphism. In particular ψ(V₀) is relatively open in W ∩ N for every open V₀ ⊆ V.
3. (Range of Dψ(z₀); (1c).) For a ∈ ℝ^{n+1} choose ε > 0 with z₀ + εta ∈ V for |t| < 1.
- γ(t) := ψ(z₀ + εta) is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps into N, γ(0) = x and γ′(0) = εDψ(z₀)a. So Dψ(z₀)a ∈ Π, since Π is a subspace.
- Dψ(z₀) is injective and dim Π = n + 1, so range Dψ(z₀) = Π.
4. (Graph map; (1d).)
- φ := ι*∘(ψ − x) is C² on V with φ(z₀) = 0, and Dφ(z₀) = ι*Dψ(z₀) is invertible (ι* is injective on Π). By the C² inverse function theorem (Mathlib ContDiffAt.to_localInverse) there are an open V₀ with z₀ ∈ V₀ ⊆ V and an open O ∋ 0 such that φ : V₀ → O is bijective with C² inverse.
- Put u(v) := ψ(φ^{-1}(v)) − x − ι v on O and u := 0 off O. Then ι*u = 0 on O, so (★) ψ(φ^{-1}(v)) = x + ι v + u(v) with u(v) ⊥ range ι.
- u is C² on O and u(0) = 0. Also Du(0) = (I − ιι*)Dψ(z₀)Dφ(z₀)^{-1} = 0, because range Dψ(z₀) = Π.
- By step 2 there is s > 0 with B_s(x) ⊆ W and N ∩ B_s(x) ⊆ ψ(V₀).
- Choose r₁ > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r₁) ⊆ U ∩ B_s(x), and put δ₂ := r₁. Then choose δ₁ ∈ (0, r₁) with ball(0, δ₁) ⊆ O, ‖Du‖ ≤ 1 and ‖u‖ < δ₂/2 on ball(0, δ₁); this uses continuity of u and Du at 0.
5. (Properties other than orientation.)
(a) closedBall(x, δ₁ + δ₂) ⊆ closedBall(x, 2r₁) ⊆ U.
(b) u(0) = 0, and u is C² on ball(0, δ₁) ⊆ O.
(c) For v ∈ ball(0, δ₁): u(v) ⊥ range ι, ‖Du(v)‖ ≤ 1, ‖u(v)‖ < δ₂/2, and x + ι v + u(v) = ψ(φ^{-1}(v)) ∈ N by (★).
(d) If ‖v‖ < δ₁, ‖h‖ < δ₂, h ⊥ range ι and q := x + ι v + h ∈ N, then ‖q − x‖² = ‖v‖² + ‖h‖², so ‖q − x‖ < 2r₁ < s. Hence q = ψ(z) with z ∈ V₀. Then φ(z) = ι*(q − x) = v, so z = φ^{-1}(v), and (★) gives h = u(v).
6. (Orientation; (1e)–(1f).) Let D := ball(0, δ₁), G(v) := x + ι v + u(v) (C² on D), and fix v ∈ D.
(6a) u maps the open set D into the closed subspace (range ι)^⊥, so Du(v)a ⊥ range ι. Hence ‖DG(v)a‖² = ‖a‖² + ‖Du(v)a‖² ≥ ‖a‖², and DG(v) is injective. Therefore J(v) > 0, and J is continuous on D.
(6b) IsOrientation at G(v) ∈ N gives Q_v = tangentSpace(N, G(v)) with dim Q_v = n + 1, of which ξN(G(v)) is a unit orientation. The curves t ↦ G(v + εta) are C¹, lie in N, pass through G(v) and have velocity εDG(v)a. So range DG(v) ⊆ Q_v, and equality holds by dimension.
(6c) Let a_i := DG(v)e_i and η(v)(α) := α(a_1, …, a_{n+1})/J(v). Gram–Schmidt gives an orthonormal basis σ of Q_v and an upper-triangular R with positive diagonal such that a_j = Σ_{i≤j} R_{ij}σ_i. Then α(a) = det R·α(σ), the Gram matrix is RᵀR, and J(v) = det R. So η(v)(α) = α(σ), and η(v) is a unit orientation of Q_v.
(6d) By orientation_sign, ξN(G(v)) = ±η(v).
(6e) Let L be the map from unit_orientation_dual in degree n+1, so η(v)(L(η(v))) = 1. Put s(v) := ξN(G(v))(L(η(v))); then s(v) = ±1, according to the sign in (6d). s is continuous on D:
- ξN is continuous on N and G is continuous from D into N, so v ↦ ξN(G(v)) is continuous;
- v ↦ η(v) is continuous, because (b_i) ↦ (α ↦ α(b_1, …, b_{n+1})) is continuous multilinear, v ↦ a_i is continuous and 1/J is continuous;
- L is continuous linear, and evaluation is continuous bilinear.
D is connected and s takes values in {±1}, so s is constant. At v = 0: G(0) = x, DG(0) = ι, a_i = τ_i, J(0) = 1 and η(0) = ξN(x), so s(0) = 1. Hence ξN(G(v)) = η(v), i.e. ξN(x + ι v + u(v))(α)·J(v) = α(ι e_1 + Du(v)e_1, …, ι e_{n+1} + Du(v)e_{n+1}) for all α and all v ∈ D.
Steps 5 and 6 give every conjunct. ∎

subproblem.title: Near any point of N ∩ U, ∂[[E]] is a multiplicity-one oriented rectifiable current of finite mass (supplied steps 2–5)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U N E : Set (Euclid P)) (ξN : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen U → InClassO n U N ξN → MeasurableSet E → E ⊆ N ∩ U → IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → x ∈ N ∩ U → ∃ (Z₀ M' : Set (Euclid P)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), IsOpen Z₀ ∧ x ∈ Z₀ ∧ Z₀ ⊆ U ∧ MeasurableSet M' ∧ M' ⊆ Z₀ ∧ CountablyRectifiable n M' ∧ μHE[n] M' ≠ ∞ ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ' (μHE[n].restrict M') ∧ (∀ᵐ w ∂(μHE[n].restrict M'), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ' w) Q) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ Z₀ → T ω = ∫ w in M', ξ' w ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) w) ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 2–5 of the supplied proof of codim1_region_density_one_dense (Simon 7.5.2 with Ch. 6, 2.35 and Ch. 3, 4.3), stated for an arbitrary x ∈ N ∩ U. Step 1 is the sibling graph_chart, and step 4 (De Giorgi) is the sibling de_giorgi.
Departure: step 3's mass bound is the accepted sibling mass_upper_bound (M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W)). This is identical in content to the first conclusion of oriented_piece_mass for R, and avoids depending on an unaccepted node.

Notation.
- H^k = μHE[k] (= volume on ℝ^k) and |·| is the coefficient norm.
- For an IMRep R = (M_R, θ_R, ξ_R), μ_R = R.measure.
- G^#β is the pull-back: (G^#β)(v)(a_1, …) = β(G(v))(DG(v)a_1, …).

Proof. Fix an IMRep R of T. InClassO gives IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) N and IsOrientation (n+1) N ξN.
0. (Chart.) graph_chart gives ι, u, δ₁, δ₂ with:
(a) closedBall(x, δ₁+δ₂) ⊆ U;
(b) u is C² on D := ball(0, δ₁);
(c) for v ∈ D: u(v) ⊥ range ι, ‖Du(v)‖ ≤ 1, ‖u(v)‖ < δ₂/2, G(v) := x + ιv + u(v) ∈ N, and ξN(G(v))(α)·J(v) = α(DG(v)e_1, …, DG(v)e_{n+1});
(d) the graph property.
Let π(w) := ι*(w − x) and p^⊥(w) := w − x − ιπ(w). Put Z := {‖π‖ < δ₁, ‖p^⊥‖ < δ₂} (open) and Z_s := Z ∩ {‖π‖ < s}. Then closure Z ⊆ closedBall(x, δ₁+δ₂) ⊆ U is compact.
(F1) N ∩ Z = G(D), by (c) and (d).
(F2) π∘G = id, and Du(v)a ⊥ range ι, so ‖a‖ ≤ ‖DG(v)a‖ ≤ √2‖a‖. Hence G is injective, DG is injective, J > 0 is continuous, and G is √2-Lipschitz on D.
(F3) N ∩ Z is relatively closed in Z: G(v_k) → w ∈ Z forces v_k → π(w) and w = G(π(w)). So G^{-1}(K) = π(K ∩ N) is compact for compact K ⊆ Z, and N ∩ Z is Borel.
1. (Local formula; supplied step 2.) F := {v ∈ D : G(v) ∈ E} is Borel, and E ∩ Z = G(F). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ Z.
(1a) dω vanishes off Z, so T(ω) = ∫_{G(F)} ξN(dω) dH^{n+1}.
(1b) SimonGMT injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (with normDet DG = J), extended from sets to integrable functions, gives ∫_{G(F)} h dH^{n+1} = ∫_F h∘G·J dv.
(1c) By 0(c), ξN(G(v))(dω(G(v)))·J(v) = (G^#dω)(v)(e_1, …, e_{n+1}).
(1d) G^#ω is a compactly supported C¹ n-form with support in D (by F3), and G^#dω = d(G^#ω) (G is C²).
(1e) Identify n-forms β with vector fields φ_β, (φ_β)_j = (−1)^{j−1}β(e_1, …, ê_j, …, e_{n+1}). Then |β| = |φ_β| and (dβ)(e_1, …, e_{n+1}) = div φ_β.
Hence (*) T(ω) = ∫_F div φ_{G^#ω} dv.
2. (Locally finite perimeter; supplied step 3.)
- Take χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ; [0,1]) with χ = 1 on (−∞, δ₂/2] and χ = 0 on [3δ₂/4, ∞), and put ζ(w) := χ(‖p^⊥(w)‖).
- Fix compact K ⊆ D, s′ < δ₁ with K ⊆ ball(0, s′), and smooth φ with tsupport ⊆ K and |φ| ≤ 1. Let β_φ be the form with φ_{β_φ} = φ, and put ω_φ(w)(a_1, …, a_n) := ζ(w)·β_φ(π(w))(ι*a_1, …, ι*a_n).
- ω_φ is smooth, and tsupport ω_φ ⊆ {π ∈ K, ‖p^⊥‖ ≤ 3δ₂/4}, a compact subset of Z_{s′} ⊆ U. So ω_φ ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
- G^#ω_φ = β_φ, since π∘G = id and ζ∘G = 1. So T(ω_φ) = ∫_F div φ by (*).
- |ω_φ| ≤ 1: in an orthonormal basis extending (ιe_i), the coefficients are ζ times those of β_φ(π(w)). The coefficient norm is basis independent, by Cauchy–Binet for the compound matrix C_n(O).
- So ω_φ is admissible for M_Z(T), and ofReal ∫_F div φ ≤ M_Z(T) ≤ μ_R(Z) ≤ μ_R(closure Z) < ∞, by mass_upper_bound and IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult.
- Thus F satisfies the hypothesis of de_giorgi with m := n and the open set D.
3. (De Giorgi; supplied step 4.)
- de_giorgi gives a Borel, rectifiable B ⊆ D with H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ D, and a Borel ν with |ν| = 1 on B, approximate tangent planes ν^⊥ H^n-a.e. on B, and ∫_F div φ = −∫_B ⟨φ, ν⟩ dH^n.
- Put ξ_F(v)(β) := −⟨φ_β, ν(v)⟩. If σ is orthonormal in ν(v)^⊥ with det[ν(v), σ] = −1, expanding det[φ_β, σ] gives β(σ) = −⟨φ_β, ν(v)⟩. So ξ_F(v) is a unit orientation of ν(v)^⊥, and it is Borel.
- Hence (**) ∫_F div φ_β = ∫_B ξ_F(β) dH^n for C¹ forms β with compact support in D.
4. (Multiplicity-one representation; supplied step 5.) Put D′ := ball(0, δ₁/2), Z₀ := Z_{δ₁/2}, B′ := B ∩ D′ and M′ := G(B′) = {w ∈ N ∩ Z : π(w) ∈ B′}.
(4a) Z₀ is open, x ∈ Z₀ ⊆ U, M′ ⊆ Z₀, and M′ is Borel.
(4b) Take B′ ⊆ B₀ ∪ ⋃F_j(ℝ^n) with H^n(B₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz, and a Lipschitz extension G̃ of G|_D. Then M′ ⊆ G̃(B₀) ∪ ⋃(G̃∘F_j)(ℝ^n), so M′ is rectifiable.
(4c) H^n(M′) ≤ 2^{n/2}H^n(B ∩ closedBall(0, δ₁/2)) < ∞.
(4d) For v ∈ B′ with ξ_F(v)(β) = β(σ), put J′(v) := (det[⟨DG(v)σ_i, DG(v)σ_j⟩])^{1/2} > 0 and ξ′(G(v))(α) := α(DG(v)σ_1, …, DG(v)σ_n)/J′(v), i.e. Λ_nDG(v)ξ_F(v)/|Λ_nDG(v)ξ_F(v)|; set ξ′ := 0 off M′.
- By Gram–Schmidt (as in graph_chart (6c)), each ξ′(w) is a unit orientation of the n-plane DG(v)(ν(v)^⊥).
- ξ′ is Borel, being continuous in π(w), DG(π(w)) and ν(π(w)), hence AE-strongly measurable.
- |ξ′(w)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ for an orthonormal τ.
(4e) Representation. Let tsupport ω ⊆ Z₀. Then β := G^#ω has compact support in D′, and by (*) and (**):
 T(ω) = ∫_{B′} ξ_F((G^#ω)(v)) dH^n = ∫_{B′} ξ′(G(v))(ω(G(v)))·J′(v) dH^n(v).
Now apply the area formula on the rectifiable set B′ (Simon Ch. 3, 2.3–2.6). For the injective Lipschitz C¹ map G, the Jacobian along T_vB′ = T_vB = ν(v)^⊥ (H^n-a.e.; D′ is open) is J′(v). This gives T(ω) = ∫_{M′} ξ′(w)(ω(w)) dH^n(w); the integrand is bounded and H^n(M′) < ∞.
This gives every conclusion with Z₀, M′ and ξ′. ∎
proof_key_steps: graph_chart: N ∩ Z is the graph G(D) of u over D ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}, and ξN∘G·J is the G-pushforward of e_1∧…∧e_{n+1}.
Area formula and pull-back: T(ω) = ∫_F div φ_{G^#ω} with F = G^{-1}(E).
The test forms ζ·π^#β_φ together with mass_upper_bound for an IMRep show that F has locally finite perimeter in D.
de_giorgi: ∫_F div φ_β = ∫_B ξ_F(β) dH^n, with B rectifiable and tangent planes ν^⊥.
Area formula on B′ = B ∩ D′: T = ∫_{M′} ξ′(ω) dH^n with M′ = G(B′) Borel, rectifiable, H^n(M′) < ∞, and ξ′ unit orientations.

audit.reason: The projected test forms establish locally finite perimeter before De Giorgi is invoked. The graph and rectifiable area formulas then yield the finite Borel multiplicity-one representation, including measurability and unit orientations. Its exact conclusion supplies the representation needed by the selected parent's assembly.
